content:
{'translation': "Argentine, led by the king of football Messi and aiming to defend their title, face Spain, another team beloved by Hong Kong fans. The championship decider took place in the early hours of today (the 20th) at three o'clock. While the match was broadcast live on free-to-air television at home, large numbers of Hong Kong fans still stayed out all night, gathering in shopping malls and bars to watch their beloved teams compete for the trophy."}

{'translation': "Before three o'clock in the early morning, fans had already packed the scene at Olympian City. The atmosphere was electric, with fans wearing jerseys, waving the national flags of the teams they supported and holding various fan paraphernalia, ready for this once-every-four-years World Cup final showdown."}

{'translation': 'Spain enjoyed more possession, while Argentina held a solid defensive line. The first half ended goalless at 0-0. In the second half, Spain took control of the match, launching attacks with several threatening shots. In stoppage time, at the 92nd minute, Enzo Fernández received a second yellow card followed by a red and was sent off.'}

{'translation': 'In the 96th minute, Spain won another free kick just outside the penalty area. Yamal took the shot, and Martínez saved it. The second-half score remained 0-0, with Argentina failing to register a single shot on goal in the 90 minutes. The match went to extra time, with Argentina down to ten men. In the 95th minute of extra time, Nico Williams found the net, but the goal was disallowed due to a prior foul by Meríno.'}

{'translation': "In the first half, Spain pressed Argentina hard and enjoyed longer periods of possession, while Argentina's defence held firm. Argentina occasionally launched counter-attacks, but failed to pose much threat to Spain before the water break. In the 38th minute, Spain's Oyarzabal took a shot from just outside the box but failed to break the deadlock. Around the 40th minute, Argentina's Lisandro Martínez received the first yellow card of the match."}

{'translation': 'Right at the start of the second half, Argentina\'s defence committed a serious error. Spain\'s forwards won the ball high up the pitch through pressing, but failed to find the net. In the 51st minute, a serious clash erupted on the pitch. Argentina\'s Leandro pushed a Spanish player down during the scuffle, prompting Spanish fans at the scene to become emotional and shout "Red card!"'}

{'translation': 'In the 59th minute, Spain won a free kick. Argentina cleared the danger successfully, and Spain brought on Ferran Torres among others. In the 66th minute, Yamal crossed from the by-line, and Ferran Torres headed the ball on target, only for goalkeeper Martínez to gather it.'}

{'translation': 'Faced with what was so far the closest chance of the match, Spanish fans at the scene could not help but shout "Oh no!" and "So close!", deeply regretting Spain\'s failure to score, while also cheering "Well played!" to express their satisfaction with Spain\'s performance.'}

{'translation': 'In the 82nd minute, Argentina\'s Enzo Fernández received a yellow card, and in stoppage time at the 92nd minute, he was shown a second yellow followed by a red and sent off. Some Spanish fans at the scene stood up and shouted "Serves him right!" and "That red card was deserved!", while Argentine fans on the other side expressed their displeasure with the referee\'s decision, saying "That\'s disputable" and "Are you kidding me?".'}

{'translation': 'In stoppage time, at the 96th minute, Spain won another free kick just outside the box. Yamal took the shot, and Martínez saved it. Faced with Spain\'s relentless attacking pressure, compounded by Argentina being reduced to ten men during stoppage time, a match already dominated by Spain became even more one-sided. Some Argentine fans shouted "Hold on!" hoping Argentina could hold out until the penalty shootout stage.'}

{'translation': 'In the 95th minute of extra time, Nico Williams found the net, and some Spanish fans rushed to the big screen to celebrate, but the goal was ruled out for a prior foul by Meríno. Then in the 105th minute, Spanish fans once again rushed to the screen to set off confetti cannons in celebration, shouting "Let\'s go!" and "Finally!"'}

{'translation': 'Ultimately Spain defeated Argentina 1-0. Large numbers of Spanish fans, both adults and children, all wearing Spain jerseys, raised replica World Cup trophies aloft and cheered in celebration together.'}

{'translation': 'Spanish fan Mr. Yuan believed Spain\'s performance in the final was "quite good, they just played their normal game", but felt that "their finishing was still a bit lacking", having failed to convert several chances.'}

{'translation': 'Argentine fan Mr. Cao also hoped that in the future there would be broadcast events for matches such as the UEFA Champions League final or other cup competitions, believing that the atmosphere at these large-scale screening events "would definitely be even better". As for Argentina\'s performance in the final, Mr. Cao said "I\'m satisfied with this edition", having not expected before the World Cup that Argentina "could reach the final stage again". He believed Argentina\'s spirit of unity remained, saying "it\'s the team spirit that holds this Argentina side together".'}
